goals.title: Attract-Mode Game Select Menu
goals.summary: The Mandalorian ships with a whole second rule set behind the attract-mode flippers, and nothing on the cabinet points to it. A group can turn an ordinary game into a shared hunt, a team battle, a punishing hard mode, or a straight run at the final wizard mode.
instructions: During attract mode, with no game in progress, hold both flipper buttons together
Keep holding until a menu appears on the display
Competition plays like Standard but makes awards deterministic, switches extra balls off, and takes away the Child mystery award
Cooperation shares progress between 2 to 4 players
Team Play splits the players 2 vs 2, 3 vs 1, or 2 vs 1

Impossible Play strips out ball saves and extra balls, tightens every multiball, pays less Beskar, locks Armor out of the Foundry, and sticks each flipper up for about two and a half seconds after you press it
Monster Play puts player one on Impossible Play rules as the Monster while all other players are set to Standard
Challenge Mode drops you straight into the You Have What I Want wizard mode
DJ Mixer is a jukebox for the music in the machine rather than a way to play
goals.reward: Standard, Competition, Cooperation, Team Play, Impossible Play, Monster Play, Challenge Mode, and a DJ Mixer jukebox

goals.title: Building Your Equipment Loadout
goals.summary: Five pieces of gear change what you can do with a ball in play. Four of them sit waiting behind the action button until you spend them; the fifth just works in the background. Collecting them is the easy half. The hard half is picking the moment - hold the rifle a beat too long and a rescue turns into a drain.
instructions: Gather gear four ways. The Foundry stocks all five pieces for Beskar. During Scope, the scoop/U-turn award tries to hand you two pieces at once. The Child's random award can also give equipment, and restarting Ambush twice pays out the Flamethrower.
Armour is the odd one out - there is no button press. It simply adds time to the ball save, in single-ball play and in multiball.
Amban Rifle: press the action button during any multiball to put another ball into play. The button does not light green for it until the multiball's opening ball save has run out.
Whistling Birds: press the action button during a running mission to collect the shots that are lit at that moment.

Flamethrower: press and hold the action button. Shots catch fire one at a time, beginning at the right orbit and travelling leftward across the playfield, and the spread stops the instant you release. A burning shot pays double the next time you hit it, and hitting it puts the fire out.
Rising Phoenix, also called the Jet Pack: press the action button to finish the Encounter level you are on outright. On Premium and LE machines it also levels the mini playfield.
goals.reward: Five equipment pieces with distinct effects: four action-button powers plus a passive ball-save extension

goals.title: Foundry Prices and the Question Mark
goals.summary: Beskar is the currency and the Foundry is where it becomes an advantage. The catch is built-in inflation: every item you buy raises its own price for the next time you want it, so the order you spend in matters as much as the total you bank. One slot on the board is a flat-rate gamble that ignores the price list entirely.
instructions: Bank Beskar. Hunter and Scope are the two main earners; the Child also hands out Beskar as one of its random awards. Collecting Beskar from any of those lights the Foundry.

Learn the price list. Lighting Scope costs 75 and lighting an Encounter 100. Each of the four action-button items - Whistling Birds, Rising Phoenix, Flamethrower, Amban Rifle - costs 175, as does starting the next mission. Armour is 200 and lighting Heal on an outlane is 200. Lighting the next Razor Crest multiball is 300, a +1x playfield multiplier is 500, and an extra ball is 600.
Buy in a deliberate order. Every time you trade for an item, that item's price rises roughly 50 percent for your next visit. The extra ball can only be bought once per game.

Take the question mark when the price list is not serving you. It costs a flat 100 Beskar and sets a cursor racing around the board; the action button stops it, and whatever it lands on is what you bought.

Stop the cursor on a question mark again and you get a hidden award instead: a two-ball frenzy multiball, lighting the Child, lighting Ambush, starting Hunter, or all three +1x playfield multipliers at once, which takes the playfield to 6x.
Or take Pass and bank the Beskar for a later, better-stocked visit.
goals.reward: Cheaper unlocks through smart buying order, plus a 100-Beskar gamble that can start a two-ball multiball or push the playfield to 6x

drills.title: Held Plunge, Three Shots
drills.text: Hold the left flipper in until the ball passes the C lane, then take the U-Turn, the right ramp and a final shot in quick succession. Decide the finisher before you plunge — the center ramp launches straight into a multiball, the left scoop into a mission.

drills.title: Uplift Target Taps
drills.text: Hit the hanging ship target directly, three times, then take the center ramp. It swings, so a glancing hit does nothing — aim through it rather than at it.

drills.title: Three Blues, Then Collect
drills.text: Take the U-Turn, the left 2X target and the right ramp in whatever order the ball gives you, then collect at the left inlane inside the short window. The collect is the part people miss — line the inlane up before you make the third shot.

drills.title: Left Ramp Rhythm
drills.text: Shoot the left ramp, take the return off the right inlane, shoot it again, and keep the rhythm rather than re-aiming each time. Long ramp counts on a timer are what several of this game's requirements come down to, and rhythm beats aiming shot by shot.

drills.title: Mini-Playfield Control
drills.text: Ride the Encounter deck out instead of flailing at it — keeping the ball alive up there is what finishes the bonus level. Take the six standups in whatever order the deck offers them, and save an equipment award for the wave you keep losing.

drills.title: Hunter Orbit Loop
drills.text: Complete the left standup bank, roll the lit inlane to start the timer, then take the flashing orbit and the opposite orbit before it runs out. Both orbits inside one short window is the whole shape of it, so pick your first orbit as the inlane rolls.

actionButton.label: Action Button
actionButton.how: The lockdown bar button is where your gear sits. Four of the five items you buy at the Foundry wait behind it and its color tells you which one is ready to spend. Collecting the gear is the easy half; picking the moment is the hard half, because a wasted press costs you the item until you earn another.

uses.what: Amban Rifle adds a ball. The button will not light green for it until the opening ball save has run out.
Whistling Birds collects every flashing shot at once, and lit jackpots too during a multiball.

uses.when: Before a big shot in single-ball play
uses.what: Hold for the Flamethrower: fire spreads right to left and stops when you release. Each burning shot pays double once.
Rising Phoenix finishes the current level outright; on Premium and LE it also levels the mini playfield.

uses.when: Question mark bought at the Foundry
uses.what: Stops the racing selector — whatever it lands on is what you walk away with.

howItPlays.objective: Play the Mandalorian hunting bounties across the galaxy with the Child along for the ride. Take Missions and Encounters, build the three Razor Crest Multiballs, spend Beskar at the Foundry for gear, and work toward the wizard mode This Is The Way.
loop: Shoot the left and right ramps to light a Mission, start it at the left scoop, and chase its flashing shots on the timer.
Tap the Razor Crest uplift target to qualify a multiball, set which one loads next at the Boba Fett targets, and start it at the center ramp.
Light Scope, Hunter, and Green off their shots to stack up to a 6X playfield, then fire the Flamethrower to double your biggest collect.
Earn Beskar from the Hunter loop and mystery awards, then spend it at the Foundry for equipment that sits behind the action button.
Clear the three mini-wizards -- all three Razor Crest Multiballs, all three Encounters, and all five Missions -- to light This Is The Way.

lights.name: Mission Ramps & Scoop
lights.lit: The Chapter and Helix ramps light to arm a bounty Mission; hit one and then the other in any order and the left scoop lights to begin it.
lights.flashing: Inside a Mission the next shot flashes yellow and cyan -- that is the one paying the rising combo value if you chain it quickly.
lights.then: Start the Mission at the scoop and chase the flashing shots on its timer. Play any two Missions in a game and the Extra Ball lights; finish all five to clear one of the three doors into This Is The Way.

lights.name: Razor Crest Multiball
lights.lit: The Razor Crest uplift target lights to qualify a Razor Crest Multiball, and the two Boba Fett targets set which of the three -- Ice Spider, Jetpack, or Pirates -- loads up next.
lights.flashing: During the multiball the U-Turn flashes for the Super Jackpot once you have banked the purple shots.
lights.then: Tap the uplift target a few times, start the multiball at the center ramp, build the Super on the purple shots, then take it at the U-Turn with the Flamethrower firing so that one shot lands doubled. Play all three multiballs to clear Precious Cargo.

lights.name: Blue / Orange / Green Multipliers
lights.lit: Three playfield multipliers stack: Blue from finishing Scope at the ramps, Orange from clearing the Hunter bank, and Green from the two Boba Fett targets, running 6X when all three are lit together.
lights.then: Blue and Orange hold for a stretch while Green is short and the only one you can start mid-multiball, so save Green for last. With all three live, start a multiball and fire the Flamethrower to push a single collect toward twelve times its base.

lights.name: Hunter Return Lanes
lights.lit: Clearing the Hunter standup bank lights one return lane to start Hunter; roll through the lit inlane and the mode runs on a short timer while you trade the two orbits.

control.effect: a tap of either flipper button swaps which inlane is lit, so you can slide the lit return under whichever inlane the ball is dropping toward and start Hunter without waiting for one exact feed
control.when: Hunter lit, before the ball reaches a return lane

lights.then: Line the lit inlane up with the ball and roll through to start Hunter, then shoot the flashing orbit and the opposite orbit to finish it for a pile of Beskar and a fresh Orange multiplier -- and the whole loop is repeatable.

lights.name: Encounter Mini-Playfield
lights.lit: The Chapter ramp insert flashes red when an Encounter is ready, and once you begin it the left-ramp shots divert the ball up onto the Encounter mini-playfield.
lights.flashing: A flashing red left-ramp insert means the next Encounter is qualified and waiting to start.
lights.then: Clear three waves of targets up top, keeping the ball alive with the tilting mini-flipper, to finish the bonus level. Complete all three Encounters to open You Have What I Want.

lights.name: Ambush Hurry-Up
lights.lit: With no mode running, a ring of shots lights briefly around the U-Turn, and catching two of them starts Ambush.
lights.flashing: During Ambush the U-Turn flashes to lock the countdown, then the ramps flash white to pump the value up.
lights.then: Lock the value at the U-Turn, feed white ramp shots to add time and points, then cash out at the right ramp once the shots have turned blue -- restarting it stacks another playfield multiplier on top.

lights.name: CHILD Lanes & HEAL
lights.lit: Spelling C-H-I-L-D across the top lanes steps up your end-of-ball bonus multiplier, and orbit shots light HEAL at the outlanes.
lights.then: Keep HEAL lit at both outlanes as a cheap save, since there is no long ball save to lean on, and bank CHILD completions to fatten the bonus your multiplier rides on.

howItPlays.laneChangeNote: Once the Hunter bank is down and a return lane lights to start Hunter, tapping either flipper button swaps which inlane is lit. Slide it under the return the ball is taking and roll through to start the mode -- a short timer worth a pile of Beskar and a fresh Orange multiplier -- and the loop repeats.

scoring.text: Go for the Super Skill Shot -- hold the left flipper through the plunge, then hit the U-Turn, right ramp, and center ramp -- or fall back to the C-lane skill shot to light The Child. Then shoot both ramps into the left scoop to start a Mission, and keep HEAL lit at the outlanes since there is no safety net.

Stack a Mission with a Razor Crest Multiball, and light Scope, Hunter, and Green together for a 6X playfield. Farm the Hunter loop for Beskar and spend it at the Foundry, buying two adjacent items to keep the price ladder cheap.

Clear the three mini-wizards -- Precious Cargo for the three Razor Crest Multiballs, You Have What I Want for the three Encounters, and I Like Those Odds for all five Missions -- to light This Is The Way. It pays ten million and a permanent Signet multiplier, the top of the whole game.
